comparator.name: International Bachelor in Psychology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme is a three-year, 180-EC psychology bachelor with a broad common foundation in behaviour, brain, development, mental health, methods, statistics and professional skills. Students later specialise in Brain and Cognition, Clinical Psychology, Education and Development, or Work and Organisational Psychology, complete minor/exchange and elective space, and finish with a thesis. Brain and Cognition is selected neutrally as the broadest basic-science continuation of the common core.
components: Personality, biological, developmental, mental-health and cross-cultural psychology
Methods, statistics, psychodiagnostics and professional skills
Cognition, learning, mental health and applied psychology
Statistics, psychometrics, ethics and scientific communication
Brain and Cognition methods, memory and data analysis

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Cognition, perception, memory and brain function
Personality, development, social behaviour and mental health
Research methods, statistics, psychometrics and evidence evaluation
Learning, work, organisations and applied psychology
Ethics, culture, communication and the history of psychology
questions: How do biological, cognitive, developmental and social processes shape behaviour and wellbeing?
How can psychological evidence be applied responsibly in health, education and organisations?

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum combines mind, brain, behaviour, lifespan development and research, and also incorporates the Education and Development interest within a broad psychology pathway. Clinical Psychology and Work and Organisational Psychology remain coherent, feasible and materially distinct official specialisation directions. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

alternatives.label: Psychology, brain & lifespan development
alternatives.labelReason: Cognitive, biological, developmental, social and health psychology are joined to statistics, research and ethics, reflecting the programme’s broad common foundation and Brain and Cognition route.
alternatives.concept: A broad scientific psychology pathway examining mind, brain, behaviour and development across the lifespan.
progression: Introductory brain, behaviour, communication and philosophy courses precede advanced cognition, health psychology, statistics and research. Level-300 work is concentrated after disciplinary foundations. All offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Clinical, health & neuropsychology
alternatives.labelReason: Abnormal, medical, developmental, biological and cognitive psychology are combined with anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology and research methods to create a defensible non-licensure clinical-health direction.
alternatives.concept: A clinical and health psychology direction focused on mental disorders, neuropsychology, biopsychosocial health, assessment evidence and mechanisms of disease.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this curriculum adds pharmacology, biochemistry, pathology/genetics, infection/immunity and professional legal-ethical study while reducing media, sociology and philosophy content.
progression: Biological, behavioural and research foundations precede advanced pathology, pharmacology, abnormal psychology, health psychology and research synthesis. All prerequisites and semester offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Work, organisations & applied psychology
alternatives.labelReason: Behavioural science, research and health psychology are integrated with business, leadership, entrepreneurship, communication and data analysis, making workplaces and organisations the clear application setting.
alternatives.concept: A work and organisational psychology direction focused on teams, leadership, workplace wellbeing, organisational diagnosis, evidence and change.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most biomedical and cognitive-neuroscience content with business, leadership, entrepreneurship, communication and organisational courses, producing a clearly distinct applied workplace pathway.
progression: Behaviour, sociology, research and business foundations precede advanced organisational behaviour, leadership, entrepreneurship and health research. All prerequisites and semester offerings are respected.

notes.text: UCR can approximate psychology as an interdisciplinary academic pathway but cannot reproduce the comparator’s full psychodiagnostic practical sequence, clinical interviewing, specialist placement environment, professional accreditation pathway or programme-specific supervised thesis.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic International Psychology. Brain and Cognition is selected from the four official specialisations because it most directly continues the common basic-science foundation rather than because it is easiest to match at UCR.
